title: Regular scheme morphisms are detected on stalk homomorphisms
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of locally Noetherian schemes [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth]. For $x\in X$, let $f_x^\sharp:\mathcal O_{Y,f(x)}\to\mathcal O_{X,x}$ be the induced local homomorphism [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism]. Then $f$ is a regular scheme morphism [def-per-regular-scheme-morphism] if and only if $f_x^\sharp$ is a regular ring map [def-weil-pbc-g-ring] for every $x\in X$.

source.place: Tag 07R8 (lemma-regular, equivalence of (2) and (3)), with More on Algebra Tag 07C0 (lemma-regular-local in more-algebra.tex). The two equivalences identify affine-chart regularity with regularity of all induced local ring maps.

proof.text: For affine opens $U\subseteq X$, $V\subseteq Y$ with $f(U)\subseteq V$, write $B=\mathcal O_X(U)$, $A=\mathcal O_Y(V)$ and $\varphi:A\to B$ for the section map. For $x\in U$, put $y=f(x)$ and let $\mathfrak q\subset B$, $\mathfrak p\subset A$ correspond to $x,y$. The affine-open stalk lemma identifies $B_{\mathfrak q}\cong\mathcal O_{X,x}$ and $A_{\mathfrak p}\cong\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ by fractions of germs. The definition of the sheaf map gives $f_x^\sharp(a_y)=\varphi(a)_x$. Its locality gives $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$, since a local homomorphism pulls the maximal ideal back to the maximal ideal. Thus it sends $a_y/s_y$ to $\varphi(a)_x/\varphi(s)_x$; under these isomorphisms it is exactly $\varphi_{\mathfrak q}:A_{\mathfrak p}\to B_{\mathfrak q}$.

source.place: Tag 01HV, lemma-spec-sheaves (6), and Tag 01HB, definition-locally-ringed-space; compatibility of section maps and germs.

proof.text: Suppose $f$ is regular. Fix $x\in X$. Choose an affine neighborhood $V$ of $f(x)$ and an affine neighborhood $U$ of $x$ contained in the open set $f^{-1}(V)$; both exist because the affine opens of a scheme form a basis of its topology. The affine criterion gives that $\varphi:A\to B$ is regular. The ring $B$ is Noetherian by the affine-open locally-Noetherian lemma, so the implication (1) to (2) of the regular-local-maximal lemma applies: $\varphi_{\mathfrak q}$ is regular. Step 1 identifies its source, target and fraction formula with the stalk map. Applying invariance of regular ring maps under these commuting ring isomorphisms shows that $f_x^\sharp$ is regular.

source.place: Tag 07C0, lemma-regular-local, (1) implies (2); affine criterion is More on Morphisms Tag 07R8. Affine neighborhoods inside an open: Schemes Tag 01IT, lemma-basis-affine-opens.

proof.text: Conversely suppose every $f_x^\sharp$ is regular. Take any affine opens $U,V$ as in Step 1. For every prime $\mathfrak q\subset B$, let $x\in U$ be its point. Step 1 and invariance under the inverse commuting ring isomorphisms give that $\varphi_{\mathfrak q}:A_{\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)}\to B_{\mathfrak q}$ is regular. Since $B$ is Noetherian by the affine-open locally-Noetherian lemma, implication (2) to (1) of the regular-local-maximal lemma gives that $\varphi$ is regular. This holds for every such pair $U,V$, so the affine criterion gives that $f$ is regular. If $X$ is empty, the same proof uses the empty family of primes and all pointwise conditions are vacuous.

source.place: Tag 07C0, lemma-regular-local, (2) implies (1); More on Morphisms Tag 07R8, (3) implies (2).
